scopeOutcomes.qualification: The editions overview places core detection, Exposure Analytics, Detection Studio and TIM in Essentials, with native SOAR and UEBA in Premier. The 8.8 licensing page requires an underlying Platform license and adds no ingestion capacity. It states 30-day Essentials and 90-day Premier trials, paid-Essentials reversion, expiry limitations, the search-head-cluster display exception and a Cloud Connected Premier trial UI showing Essentials despite continuing connectivity. Pricing model headings do not establish eligibility for every ES deployment. Contract entitlement, activity-model deployment scope, pairing and account activation remain separate.

readerReview.question: Does buying ES increase ingest capacity, and how long are the edition trials?
readerReview.answer: ES is used with Splunk Enterprise or Cloud Platform and does not add ingestion capacity.
readerReview.reportAnswer: ES is used with Splunk Enterprise or Cloud Platform and does not add ingestion capacity.

scopeOutcomes.qualification: The 8.7 release notes retain September 2 for 8.7.0, October 1 for 8.7.1, and October 23 for 8.7.2. The Connector Builder enhancement is labeled Premier in 8.7.1. The 8.8 release entry is General Availability dated November 4, with per-agent release stages remaining separate. The exact feature table places Entity posture, profile, actions, Entity Analysis and fine-grained RBAC in Essentials, inherited by Premier. UEBA dataset management, insider-threat annotations, broker HA and private-CA pairing have their own Premier rows. Current Exposure Analytics summaries and configured entity follow-up actions match these passages; no universal autonomous action or blanket AI GA was inferred.
